facts.claim: An eval is a test for an AI system: give it an input, then apply grading logic to its output to measure success.
Model outputs vary between runs, so each attempt at a test case is counted as one trial.
Anthropic suggests 20 to 50 simple test cases drawn from real failures as a good start, including failures users reported.
A reference solution is a known working output that passes every grader. It shows the case can be solved and that the graders are set up right.
Hamel Husain advises removing all friction from looking at your data, and updating tests as new failures show up in it.
Code graders are fast, cheap, objective and repeatable, but brittle: a valid answer that does not match the expected pattern exactly fails.
Model graders are flexible and catch nuance, but they vary from run to run, cost more than code, and need checking against people to be accurate.
People are the gold standard for grading, but they are expensive and slow.
In a 2023 study, GPT-4 as a judge agreed with people's preferences over 80% of the time, about as often as people agreed with each other.
Raw agreement can mislead when most cases pass or most fail; Hamel Husain suggests also tracking precision and recall.
Position bias is a model judge's habit of favouring an answer for where it sits, such as first, over what it says.
Verbosity bias is a model judge's habit of favouring longer answers, even when they are less clear or accurate.
One fix for position bias: ask the judge twice with the answers swapped, and count a win only when the same answer wins both times; otherwise call it a tie.
An agent's outcome is checked in its environment, not taken from what it says: for a booking, whether the reservation exists in the database.
Anthropic notes it is often better to grade what an agent produced than the exact steps it took, since a fixed step list is brittle.
pass@k is the chance that at least one of k tries is correct.
pass^k is the chance that all k tries succeed.

The τ-bench paper proposed pass^k to measure how reliably an agent behaves over repeated tries, and in 2024 found the agents it tested, gpt-4o among them, inconsistent: pass^8 under 25% on its retail tasks.
